setupText: The deadline for sending your lunch order is 10 a.m.
text: The deadline for sending your lunch order is 10 a.m. Which action meets the deadline?
options: Send the order by ten.
Start choosing lunch at 10:15.
Send the order when lunch arrives.
Wait until ten before reading the menu.
answer: Send the order by ten.
explanation: A deadline is the latest time an action must be completed.

Starting after ten is already too late for this deadline.
Delivery happens after ordering; it does not meet the stated sending time.
A deadline is the latest time an action must be completed.
The order must be sent by ten, not merely considered then.

setupText: After repairing our printer, the engineer emailed an invoice for $80.
text: After repairing our printer, the engineer emailed an invoice for $80. What is this document for?
options: confirming that we have paid
offering us a new printer for $80
recording our request for a repair
telling us what we need to pay
answer: telling us what we need to pay
explanation: An invoice lists charges and requests payment; it is not itself proof of payment.

rationales.telling us what we need to pay: An invoice lists charges and requests payment; it is not itself proof of payment.
rationales.confirming that we have paid: A receipt normally confirms payment; an invoice requests it.
rationales.offering us a new printer for $80: This invoice charges for the completed repair, not a proposed new purchase.
rationales.recording our request for a repair: The request came before the work; this document gives the charge afterwards.

setupText: Nora checks the packing team's work each day. She is their supervisor.
text: Nora checks the packing team's work each day. She is their supervisor. Which description fits Nora's role?
options: She buys the boxes they pack.
She visits to learn about their jobs.
She oversees their day-to-day work.
She delivers supplies from another company.
answer: She oversees their day-to-day work.
explanation: A supervisor checks and directs the work of other people.

A buyer purchases goods; a supervisor oversees the work.
A visitor observing the work is not necessarily responsible for it.
rationales.She delivers supplies from another compa: A supplier provides materials, not day-to-day supervision.
A supervisor checks and directs the work of other people.

setupText: The careers adviser can see me at three. I have an appointment with her.
text: The careers adviser can see me at three. I have an appointment with her. What has been arranged?
options: a job she has already offered me
a time for us to meet
a class that anyone can join
a deadline for paying her
answer: a time for us to meet
explanation: An appointment is an agreed meeting at a particular time.

rationales.a job she has already offered me: An appointment to meet is not a job offer.
rationales.a time for us to meet: An appointment is an agreed meeting at a particular time.
rationales.a class that anyone can join: This appointment is arranged with the speaker, not an open class.
rationales.a deadline for paying her: A meeting time is not a payment deadline.

setupText: My usual workday ends at five, but yesterday I worked overtime until seven.
text: My usual workday ends at five, but yesterday I worked overtime until seven. What was different yesterday?
options: I arrived after my usual start time.
I took extra time off.
I did the same work more quickly.
I worked beyond my usual hours.
answer: I worked beyond my usual hours.
explanation: Overtime is work outside the normal working hours.

Overtime is work outside the normal working hours.
Arriving late is not what overtime means; the sentence concerns extra hours at the end.
Time off is time not working, whereas overtime adds work.
Overtime describes additional working time, not speed.

sentence: What information does a schedule give?
setupText: The work schedule now shows cleaning at eight and deliveries at nine.
taskText: What information does a schedule give?
text: The work schedule now shows cleaning at eight and deliveries at nine. What information does a schedule give?
options: when activities are planned to happen
how much each activity costs
how well each activity was done
why each activity was chosen
answer: when activities are planned to happen
explanation: A schedule sets out planned activities and their times.

rationales.how much each activity costs: Costs belong in a budget, not necessarily a schedule.
rationales.how well each activity was done: A schedule plans activities; it does not assess their quality.
rationales.when activities are planned to happen: A schedule sets out planned activities and their times.
rationales.why each activity was chosen: Reasons may be explained separately; a schedule primarily organizes timing.

setupText: The job offers a salary of $30,000 a year, paid monthly.
text: The job offers a salary of $30,000 a year, paid monthly. What does the salary describe?
options: the money I must pay for training
the regular amount I earn from the job
the money customers spend at the business
the extra gift I receive at the end of the year
answer: the regular amount I earn from the job
explanation: Salary is regular pay for employment; an annual amount may be paid in monthly parts.

rationales.the money I must pay for training: A salary is paid to the worker, not charged to them.
rationales.the regular amount I earn from the job: Salary is regular pay for employment; an annual amount may be paid in monthly parts.
rationales.the money customers spend at the busines: Customer spending is business income, not the employee's salary.
rationales.the extra gift I receive at the end of t: An extra award is a bonus; salary is regular pay.

setupText: Before using the new coffee machine, staff will have training.
text: Before using the new coffee machine, staff will have training. What should staff expect?
options: a decision about who gets the job
instruction and practice in using it
a record of their monthly pay
a review of last year's sales
answer: instruction and practice in using it
explanation: Workplace training develops the knowledge and skills needed for a task.

rationales.a decision about who gets the job: Choosing new employees is recruitment; these staff are already employed.
rationales.a record of their monthly pay: A pay record is not training.
rationales.a review of last year's sales: A sales review examines results, not how to operate the new machine.
rationales.instruction and practice in using it: Workplace training develops the knowledge and skills needed for a task.

sentence: Which description of 'employer' is correct here?
setupText: The museum employs Jo as a guide. Jo is an employee; the museum is her employer.
taskText: Which description of 'employer' is correct here?
text: The museum employs Jo as a guide. Jo is an employee; the museum is her employer. Which description of 'employer' is correct here?
options: the visitors Jo shows around
the person Jo works beside
the organization that gives Jo paid work
the guide who receives the pay
answer: the organization that gives Jo paid work
explanation: An employer employs someone; an employee works for that employer.

rationales.the visitors Jo shows around: The visitors use the museum's service but do not employ Jo.
rationales.the person Jo works beside: A fellow worker is a colleague, not necessarily an employer.
rationales.the organization that gives Jo paid work: An employer employs someone; an employee works for that employer.
rationales.the guide who receives the pay: Jo receives pay as the employee; the question asks about the employer.

sentence: Which task belongs to customer service in this situation?
setupText: A passenger cannot find her booking. The airline's customer service team helps her.
taskText: Which task belongs to customer service in this situation?
text: A passenger cannot find her booking. The airline's customer service team helps her. Which task belongs to customer service in this situation?
options: helping the passenger solve her booking problem
repairing the aircraft's engine
planning the pilots' work hours
choosing uniforms for employees
answer: helping the passenger solve her booking problem
explanation: Customer service assists people using a business's goods or services.

rationales.helping the passenger solve her booking: Customer service assists people using a business's goods or services.
rationales.repairing the aircraft's engine: That is technical maintenance, not assistance with this customer's booking.
rationales.planning the pilots' work hours: Staff scheduling is different from helping a passenger.
rationales.choosing uniforms for employees: Internal purchasing does not address the passenger's problem.

setupText: I bought stamps for the office. Accounts asked for the receipt.
text: I bought stamps for the office. Accounts asked for the receipt. Which document do they want?
options: a list of stamps I might buy next week
a record showing what I paid for the stamps
a note asking the post office for a price
a form asking permission to buy stamps
answer: a record showing what I paid for the stamps
explanation: A receipt records a completed purchase and payment.

rationales.a list of stamps I might buy next week: A shopping list records intended purchases, not completed payment.
rationales.a note asking the post office for a pric: A price request comes before payment and does not prove it.
rationales.a form asking permission to buy stamps: Permission is not evidence that the purchase took place.
rationales.a record showing what I paid for the sta: A receipt records a completed purchase and payment.

setupText: The shop refunded the customer $25 for the returned kettle.
text: The shop refunded the customer $25 for the returned kettle. What happened to the $25?
options: The customer paid it again.
The shop added it to the price.
The shop gave it back to the customer.
The customer borrowed it from the shop.
answer: The shop gave it back to the customer.
explanation: To refund money is to return money previously paid.

A refund goes back to the customer; it is not a second charge.
To refund money is to return money previously paid.
Adding to the price increases the charge instead of returning money.
A refund returns the customer's payment; it is not a loan.

sentence: What belongs in the signature box?
setupText: The delivery form has two boxes: 'Print your name' and 'Signature.'
taskText: What belongs in the signature box?
text: The delivery form has two boxes: 'Print your name' and 'Signature.' What belongs in the signature box?
options: the company's street address
the date the parcel was sent
your name as you normally sign it
the name of the item inside
answer: your name as you normally sign it
explanation: A signature is the personal written mark or name you use to sign a document.

rationales.your name as you normally sign it: A signature is the personal written mark or name you use to sign a document.
rationales.the company's street address: An address identifies a place, not the person signing.
rationales.the date the parcel was sent: A date is separate information, not a signature.
rationales.the name of the item inside: The contents describe the delivery, not who signs for it.

sentence: What makes these clothes a uniform?
setupText: Everyone serving in this cafe wears the same green shirt and black trousers as a uniform.
taskText: What makes these clothes a uniform?
text: Everyone serving in this cafe wears the same green shirt and black trousers as a uniform. What makes these clothes a uniform?
options: They follow the cafe's common clothing style for staff.
They are the most expensive clothes available.
They are worn only during training.
They belong to the customers rather than staff.
answer: They follow the cafe's common clothing style for staff.
explanation: A uniform is specified clothing that identifies members of a group or organization.

rationales.They are the most expensive clothes avai: Price does not make clothing a uniform.
The sentence concerns everyone serving, not only trainees.
rationales.They follow the cafe's common clothing s: A uniform is specified clothing that identifies members of a group or organization.
rationales.They belong to the customers rather than: The servers wear the uniform; it is not customer clothing.

setupText: This bank has branches in three towns. I work at the Riverside branch.
text: This bank has branches in three towns. I work at the Riverside branch. What is the Riverside branch?
options: a different bank owned by its customers
the bank's full network of offices
the group that makes rules for all banks
one local office of the bank
answer: one local office of the bank
explanation: A business branch is one of its local offices or outlets.

rationales.a different bank owned by its customers: A branch belongs to the bank; the word does not indicate separate ownership.
rationales.the bank's full network of offices: One branch is one location, not the whole network.
rationales.the group that makes rules for all banks: A branch serves as part of one bank, not as a rule-making body.
rationales.one local office of the bank: A business branch is one of its local offices or outlets.

setupText: The museum advertises a position for a weekend guide.
text: The museum advertises a position for a weekend guide. What is being advertised?
options: a job someone can apply for
a place to stand during a tour
a route visitors should follow
an opinion about museum opening hours
answer: a job someone can apply for
explanation: A position in a job advertisement is a role available for employment.

rationales.a place to stand during a tour: Position can mean location, but advertising a guide position concerns employment.
rationales.a job someone can apply for: A position in a job advertisement is a role available for employment.
rationales.a route visitors should follow: A route describes movement, not the guide's job vacancy.
rationales.an opinion about museum opening hours: Position can mean viewpoint, but this advertisement names a work role.

sentence: What does the bakery plan to do?
setupText: The bakery will hire two assistants before the busy season.
taskText: What does the bakery plan to do?
text: The bakery will hire two assistants before the busy season. What does the bakery plan to do?
options: ask two assistants to leave
send two assistants on holiday
ask two assistants to pay for training
employ two assistants
answer: employ two assistants
explanation: To hire a person for work means employ that person.

rationales.ask two assistants to leave: That would reduce staff; hiring brings people into employment.
rationales.send two assistants on holiday: Leave is time away from an existing job, not hiring.
rationales.employ two assistants: To hire a person for work means employ that person.
rationales.ask two assistants to pay for training: Hiring does not mean charging applicants a training fee.

setupText: Tariq has accepted another job and will resign from the garage.
text: Tariq has accepted another job and will resign from the garage. What will Tariq do?
options: take a short break and then return
be dismissed by the garage
give up his current job officially
move to a different task at the garage
answer: give up his current job officially
focusKey: coverage-workplace-vocabulary-a2-4118:Resign versus be dismissed or take leave
explanation: To resign is to leave a position by one's own decision, usually notifying the employer.

rationales.give up his current job officially: To resign is to leave a position by one's own decision, usually notifying the employer.
rationales.take a short break and then return: A break or leave does not end the employment relationship.
rationales.be dismissed by the garage: Dismissal is the employer's action; resignation is the employee's decision.
rationales.move to a different task at the garage: Changing duties within the same employment is not resigning from it.

sentence: Which action is still to happen?
setupText: The courier collected our order this morning and will deliver it to the client this afternoon.
taskText: Which action is still to happen?
text: The courier collected our order this morning and will deliver it to the client this afternoon. Which action is still to happen?
options: taking the parcel from our office
placing the order with a supplier
wrapping the goods for travel
bringing the parcel to the client
answer: bringing the parcel to the client
explanation: Deliver means take something to its intended recipient or destination.

rationales.taking the parcel from our office: That is collection, which has already happened.
rationales.placing the order with a supplier: Ordering occurred before the courier collected the parcel.
rationales.wrapping the goods for travel: Packing prepares goods for transport; delivery is the later arrival.
rationales.bringing the parcel to the client: Deliver means take something to its intended recipient or destination.

setupText: The workshop will supply gloves, so participants do not need to bring their own.
text: The workshop will supply gloves, so participants do not need to bring their own. What will the workshop do?
options: ask participants to buy gloves elsewhere
provide gloves for participants to use
collect participants' gloves at the door
teach participants to make gloves
answer: provide gloves for participants to use
explanation: Supply means provide something needed; the sentence removes the need to bring gloves.

rationales.ask participants to buy gloves elsewhere: That conflicts with supplying gloves itself.
rationales.provide gloves for participants to use: Supply means provide something needed; the sentence removes the need to bring gloves.
rationales.collect participants' gloves at the door: Collecting their gloves would take them in, not provide them.
rationales.teach participants to make gloves: Teaching a skill is different from providing the actual equipment.
